name: diff
title: Diff
purpose: One file's change as a unified diff, with its path and how many lines were added and removed.
whenToUse: To show what a task changed in one file, before the reader decides on it.
One diff per file. For several files, list them and put each diff in a row disclosure.
The counts alone, ds-diff__counts, beside a file's name in a list row or a disclosure summary.
whenNotToUse: For a file's contents with no change, or for a command's output. Use the code block.
For two versions side by side. This component is unified only, which is what fits a phone.
For a change to prose that the reader edits in place. Show the text itself.
accessibility: Use a figure. Its figcaption, ds-diff__header, holds the path in a code element and the counts. Leave the header out when the diff sits under a summary that already shows both.
Write each count as a sign and a number followed by a ds-diff__label span that finishes it in words, such as +7 and lines added. The label is hidden from sight and read by a screen reader.
The body is a pre with tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label naming the file, so it can take focus and the arrow keys scroll it sideways. The page itself never scrolls sideways.

Each line is a ds-diff__line holding a ds-diff__sign cell and a ds-diff__text cell. Use an ins element for an added line and a del element for a removed one, with the plus or minus as the sign. A context line and a hunk header are spans, with a space as the sign.
Never leave out the sign. The shading alone does not mark a line for someone who cannot tell the colours apart.

While the diff is fetched, set aria-busy="true" on the figure and put a ds-diff__note with role="status" in place of the body. When it fails, use a note with role="alert" that says why. The stylesheet adds the failure's icon.
When a file changed with no line to show, or the diff is cut short, say so in a plain ds-diff__note.
